457 of 8,001 offers dropped (54.2 fps), every one for the geometry; at 130 MHz 398 (the board's "more drops at 125").
Geometry x0.9 leaves 315, x0.8 169, x0.7 7. The rasteriser x0.9 changes nothing. Six of the 801 frames have a
different triangle count from the model in the geometry bench (all from 4,990 on); base-tree behaviour, not chased.

**4. Where the geometry's time goes** (kernel trace in a copy with the engine's owner flags public; 30 of Scud Race's
90 frames over a vblank):
- The engine is busy 84.5%; idle with a machine asking (external-port loads, hand-overs) 7.3%; idle with nobody
  asking (the walker or the decoder) 8.2%.
- Kernels: SETUP4 24.0%, TL 19.8%, MM 7.0%, CULLU 6.6%, MODEL 5.7%, CULLT 5.0%, PROJ 4.9%, TL3 4.9%, PROJ3 4.3%.
  About 21,000 kernels a frame, each ending 14 clocks after its last issue (the last write), about 11% of the frame.
- The per-node path is about a third of these frames: the node's matrix in through the external port (16 clocks),
  MM (60 clocks for 16 operations), CULLU (57 for 4), CULLT (43 for 3), and 110 clocks on average from one node's
  CULLT to the next node's MM. Its chain is Supermodel's order of eleven dependent multiply-adds a node.
- Not memory: all three ports at 2-3 clocks take 2.9% off; VROM at 14-42 adds 2.7%; the output port never stalling
  0.1%. R127's VROM overlap holds; a VROM cache would buy at most those few percent (and R127 priced it at a third
  of the M10K).

**5. Where the rasteriser's time goes** (heavy race frames, a profile of wires only): the pixel stage has a pair 58.8%
of the replay (a pixel into the cache 30.4%, the cache refusing 30.7%); without one 41.2%, of it the front busy with
no span 22.0% (the edge waiting for the divider 13.4%, the first-row product 5.8%). Bounds on the 144 heaviest race
frames, against the base at 31-54:

| variant | mean replay | frames over a vblank (83) |
|---|---|---|
| the divider in one clock (measurement only) | -0.35% | 82 |
| the first-row product in one clock (measurement only) | -0.13% | 83 |
| both in one clock | -0.47% | 82 |
| every port at 2-3 clocks | -14.6% | 3 |
| 16 texture fills in flight (FB 4) | -12.3% | 14 |
| 64 KiB texture cache (SB 9) | -4.7% | 63 |

On the whole race FB 4 takes the dual -5.5% case's rasteriser drops from 154 to 12 at 31-54. VF3's 50 heaviest: FB 4
-11.7% (its 5 frames over 0.95 vblank -32%), SB 9 -4.6%. The front is not the limit: the per-pair intake (a field a
clock) and the divider both take about 24 clocks a pair and the 256-pair queue decouples them; making either instant
moves nothing. The texture fills are.

**6. But the bench's texture port is latency-bound, and the board's is bandwidth-bound.** R82's probe at 100 MHz had
773 MB/s at 8 reads in flight (97% of the port's 800) and 794 at 16, the median latency 26 -> 58 clocks. At 125 MHz
the port peaks at 1 GB/s, and 8 reads of 32 bytes at the unloaded 140 ns would carry 1.8 GB/s, so 8 fills in flight
already fill the port. FB 4's bench gain is the bench's latency model, and on the board it would mainly lengthen the
queue the geometry's VROM bursts wait in (DDR_MAXQ 8 is R101's cap for that), which D-48 does not allow. The bench
also gives the store, the layer and the textures a port each: a heavy race frame moves about 4.9 MB of texture
lines, 2.9 MB of store reads (each record read again in every band it covers), 1.6 MB of store writes and 0.76 MB
of layer, about 12 MB a vblank with the scan-out and VROM against the port's 17.4 MB. So where the board's
rasteriser really sits between the bench's 13-40 and 31-54 figures needs the board's overlay rows 12-15 (R101).

**7. Ranked** (frames dropped in the sampled sets at 125 MHz; ALM estimated unless built):

| rank | change | frames | cost | state |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | two set-up groups in one kernel (`SU_PAIR`) | geometry -2.0 to -3.0%; Scud Race 457 -> 422, Daytona 2 race 21 -> 10, attract 65 -> 10 | +48 ALUTs, +15 registers (about 25-30 ALM), no M10K | built, fitted |
| 2 | a kernel starting in the last one's 14-clock drain when it is another machine's and needs no external load | about -4% geometry (est.: 3,300 + 3,500 such hand-overs a heavy frame x about 17 clocks) | 100-200 ALM, a per-machine completion tracker | not built |
| 3 | 16 texture fills in flight (FB 4, DDR_MAXQ 16) | race 154 -> 12, VF3's heavy frames -32% on the bench; little on a bandwidth-bound port | about 50 ALM | measured, not taken (D-48: the VROM queue) |
| 4 | 64 KiB texture cache (SB 9) | -4.7% race, -12.5% VF3 heaviest; fewer fills, so it holds on the board | +24-32 M10K (19 free) | measured, no room |
| 5 | the geometry's engine running two kernels at once (two contexts, or the walker a node ahead) | Scud Race's 457 drops to about 7 at x0.7 | 1,000 ALM or more (est.), a redesign | not built |
| - | the front (divider, product, intake) | none | | measured |
| - | a VROM cache | at most 2.9% | a third of the M10K (R127) | not built |

**8. Built: two set-up groups in one kernel (`r3d_geo` `SU_PAIR`, default 1).** The set-up kernel is the geometry's
largest share in the frames that drop (24%) and issues on 73 of its 116 clocks; two groups' chains interleaved fill
each other's waits. TL already issues on 91% of its clocks, and the node kernels are one dependent chain, so the
set-up is the one kernel that pairs.
- `gen_ucode.py`: `k_setup_pair` builds SETUP44 (146 operations, 168 clocks against 2 x 116) and SETUP22 (94, 119
  against 2 x 110). The first group's operations sit at the single kernel's cycles (`schedule(ops, fixed)`), the
  second's in the cycles and write slots left. The second group uses registers 64-87, 24-31 and 39, which no kernel
  holds across kernels and the external port never touches (every kernel's live-ins and every external address:
  8-23, 88-105, 124-127), and its staging reads and output writes carry address bit 6. The ROM's first 630 words are
  unchanged; the new kernels are words 630-878 of the 1,024 the set-up ROM already had.
- `r3d_geo`: bit 6 selects the other half for class 3 only (the staging read address and the set-up output's write
  address). At the grant, if the other staging half is closed, of the same kind, and its output half has been sent,
  the set-up machine starts the pair kernel. The first half goes to the emitter, and its staging half back to the
  staging machine, at the clock a single kernel's would (`LEN_SETUP4 / LEN_SETUP2 + SU_EXIT`); the second at the end.
  Two Verilator assertions: every single set-up kernel leaves K_RUN exactly at its length + SU_EXIT (a planted
  SU_EXIT of 3 trips it), and nothing is written into the first half after it was handed on. 0 keeps one group a
  kernel.

*Wrong turns:*
- My first SU_PAIR handed both halves on at the pair kernel's end. On Scud Race's 801 frames the geometry was 1.58%
  shorter but 43 frames, all ~1,700-clock title frames, were up to 49 clocks slower. I took that for the first half's
  results now waiting 51 clocks longer, and moved the first group's operations to the single kernel's cycles with the
  first half handed on at the single's clock (the form kept). The title frames stayed slower, and so did three
  variants that paired only after a wait for the engine or with the staging machine stalled. The cause was the
  geometry bench: it draws every port latency and the output stall from one random stream for the whole run, so a
  frame's clocks depend on the draws of every frame before it, and any timing change reshuffles the later frames'
  latencies by tens of clocks. `R3D_RESEED=1` (tb_r3d_geo) seeds each frame's streams from its own number; with it the
  title frames are identical and no frame of any set is slower. Comparisons of per-frame geometry clocks between two
  builds made before this (here and in earlier entries) carry that noise.
- I ran FB 4 and the 64 KiB cache in the bench and only then checked them against R82's board probe; the bench's
  latency model is what made FB 4 look large.
- Two of my bench chains shared one chunk folder and overwrote each other's logs; each run now has its own.
- The divider and the first-row product looked like 19% of the heavy replay in the profile; made instant, together
  they are 0.47%.

*Next:*
- The board: Scud Race's airport long views and Daytona 2's race with `r3dp_s1`, and overlay rows 12-15 for where the
  rasteriser's replay and the DDR3 port really sit, which decides between the bench's two texture figures.
- The geometry's real lever is concurrency (rank 5): two kernels in the engine at once, or the walker a node ahead.
  Rank 2 is the cheap step toward it.
- The 64 KiB cache needs about 10 M10K found elsewhere.

**9. Addendum (2026-11-15): Sega Rally 2, and the ranking again with SU_PAIR in (D-71).** The board build `c125dp35_s1`
(dual, 125 MHz) runs every game but holds Sega Rally 2 at 30 fps about half the time. Same method, measurement
only: Supermodel's Real3D dumps every 10 frames of a scripted race (the Desert stage, 5,250-8,800) and of the
attract (1,000-6,000), the VROM from R168's bench image, the CPU from Supermodel's instructions a frame at Daytona
2's rate (R171: 3.21 clocks an instruction with the DMA poll and the DTLB handler; Rally 2 has no system-bench frames
to calibrate its own). The dumps were deleted after.
- *Wrong turn:* the first two runs were `srally2dx`. With the merged zip Supermodel loads the Deluxe clone (R168's
  finding, which I had not carried over); its VROM is not srally2's, so the dumps drew as flat sheets and stray
  decals while Supermodel's grabs looked right. Rendering a dump beside its grab showed it. The runs now use a folder
  of their own whose Games.xml has the three clones taken out; Scud Race's and Daytona 2's runs had loaded the
  intended sets.
- **Rally 2's limiter is the CPU, where it misses.** The attract's mountain run needs about 780,000 instructions a
  frame (an FP transform at 6F2E8 and a byte scan at 6D38C on top; no poll loop among them) against 383,000-430,000
  in the desert runs: 1.11 / 1.18 vblank p50 / p90 at 125 MHz single, 1.05 dual -5.5%, 1.07 at 130, so 30 fps there
  (31.2-32.5) at every clock; it needs -10% (p50) to -15% (p90). The rasteriser drops 23 of 5,001 attract offers
  (close-ups and the ranking, to 1.44 vblank); the geometry never limits (at most 0.96).
- The Desert race runs at 57.5 on these figures (CPU p50 0.53-0.60, geometry at most 0.68, rasteriser at most 0.64,
  also at 31-54). The board's half-time 30 fits stretches like the mountain on the CPU; for the Desert race itself to
  be at 30 half the time Rally 2's code would have to cost 1.7-1.8 times Daytona 2's per instruction, which only a
  system-bench run of Rally 2's game loop, or the board's frame-busy rows on that stage, can settle.
- SU_PAIR on Rally 2: geometry -4.19% on the race's 801 frames, -3.61% on the attract's 501, every frame exact,
  none slower. No frame changes.

**R186 — D-70: the fixes for R183's second bug, priced. The carry of 2 into the page compares is cured by
moving a split's +4 out of the compares' low part and into their y operand, so both compares add two terms again.
The DBAT compare has the same fault, which R183 missed, and the operand form fixes both at once. Fix A (the operand
formed by an incrementer in front of the compares) costs about 10 ALUTs but 0.65-0.85 ns on the D-cache's hit
paths, and makes them the chip's worst at −40 °C (−3.566 against c125s_s1's −3.254 ns). Fix B (the operand as a
register of its own, loaded with the +4 as the first word goes) costs 32 registers and about 20 ALUTs, and its fit's
worst is within 0.015 ns of c125s_s1's at both slow corners. Neither costs a cycle on any bench. A zero-cycle offset,
mfsr reading MEM's copy of the segment registers (S1), frees two MLABs (20 ALM of memory) but costs about as much
logic: it does not reliably pay for B. The third way, a retry only on
the carry of 2, costs a cycle in that case and puts a term on two critical paths; priced on paper, not built.**

Work in `sm3-builds/rpefix2/` (`NOTES.md`, "D-70"; trees `fa`, `fb`, `fbs` on b10 + the RPE fix for the benches;
`c125base` = 718e9e4 + `c125130-718e9e4.patch` (md5 d8a502c5), with `c125fixA`, `c125fixB`, `c125fixBS` for the
fits; `tools/mkfix.py`, `tools/mks1.py`). D-70, D-48 / D-57 (no cycle), §8.4, R124, R129 §5a, R183. Fits
`c2fa_s1`, `c2fb_s1`, `c2fbs_s1` (seed 1, single SDRAM, release, 125 MHz, as c125s_s1). Nothing committed, nothing on
the board.

*What I believed (R183 §6, D-70):*
- Only the micro-TLB's compare was wrong. The fix on the hit path would be a second compare against page − 1, and
  the one off it about +100 ALM.

*What I know now:*

**1. Where the +4 goes.** ea_x already adds the +4 with a full adder, and is right. The compares are laid out
carry-free (each bit tests x ^ y ^ K against the carry the sum K needs, from the bit below), which is exact only for
two terms. The +4 was a third term, added only in the micro-TLB's low part (`ea_lo = op_x[11:0] + op_y[11:0] + 4`),
and FFF + FFF + 4 carries 2. If the +4 is in the y operand instead, `op_c = op_y + 4 * ex_s0ok`, the compares add
op_x and op_c, the low part carries 0 or 1, and both laid-out compares are exact for every operand. ea_x keeps its
form; mx.ya (tlbie's EA) and every other user of op_y are untouched.

**2. The DBATs have the same fault.** Their compare (db_cf, R108) is carry-free too, with the block's lowest bit from
ea_x. A carry of 2 travels up while both operands' bits are 1 (1 + 1 + 2 = 4 carries 2 again), so with bits 12 up to
the block's lowest all ones in both, it reaches the DBAT's first carry-free bit. A Python model of the laid-out
DBAT compare: 6,291 of 300,000 page-crossing word splits with both low halves at FFD or above disagree with the match
on ea_x; with two terms, 0 of 200,000. The bench never made one (its DBAT check against `bat_match(ea_x)` never
fired), but a game could: a false BAT hit gives the wrong physical page, a false miss sends the access to MEM, whose
slow translation reads the BAT hit as a protection fault (a DSI). A second micro-TLB compare against page − 1 would
not have touched this; the operand form fixes it with the same change.

**3. The two fixes.**
- **A, on the hit path:** `op_c` a wire, `{op_y[31:2] + ex_s0ok, op_y[1:0]}`, a 30-bit incrementer in front of both
  compares.
- **B, off it:** `op_c` a register. It loads op_y's own D whenever op_y loads (`!ex_hold || rl_y`), and op_y + 4 on
  the edge that sets ex_s0ok (`mis_go && !m_kp`, which only an EX that holds makes), so op_c = op_y + 4 * ex_s0ok
  whenever EX holds a uop (checked every cycle).
- Both: a new check, every micro-TLB entry's hit against `du_pg == ea_x[31:12]` every cycle. The old check compared
  the laid-out compare with `sum_is`, the same arithmetic, so it could not see this.

**4. Benches** (b10 + the RPE fix + each fix):

| Bench | Fix A | Fix B |
|---|---|---|
| cpubench (test_cpu 200, test_cpu_sub 200, --snoop 2 100, ISB 1 200, fpburst, fpchain, rdy 30, D-cache seeds 1-4) | every line identical to the base: 2,119,480 / 10,471,182 / 5,426,277 / 10,499,989 / 1,548,262 / 1,340,064 / 2,551,114 cycles; D-cache 3,302,373 / 3,317,127 / 3,339,109 / 3,300,996 | the same, identical |
| `--alias` 1-3000 (the base fails 18) | PASS, 10,857,909 instructions, 34,801,291 cycles | PASS, identical |
| the other 18 profiles, 3,000 seeds each (plain, max wait 1, `--loops`, `--xpage`, `--mode 1 / 2`, `--rdy 30`, `--dlat 1`, `--fpburst`, `--fpchain`, `--mis`, `--mis --intdrop 100`, the six xpage sets, `--mis --dlat 1`) | all PASS, every line identical to the base in instructions and cycles (225,675,557 instructions, 837,705,070 cycles) | all PASS, identical to A and the base |
| planted fault: the check alone, without the fix | `--alias` 470, 741, 766, 1926 each stop on it ("micro-TLB 3: the compare against ea_x's page (60364002)") | |
| `quartus_map --analyze_file` (17.0), ppc_core.sv in all four trees | successful, 0 errors | successful, 0 errors |

No cycle changes anywhere but in the runs that met the bug, which now finish.

**5. The fits** (seed 1, single SDRAM, release, 125 MHz; c125s_s1 is the same tree without a fix):

| | c125s_s1 | c2fa_s1 (A) | c2fb_s1 (B) | c2fbs2_s1 (B + S1) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| setup slow 100 °C, ns (TNS) | −3.468 (−8,797) | −3.429 (−9,151) | −3.474 (−8,151) | −2.956 (−5,704) |
| setup slow −40 °C, ns (TNS) | −3.254 (−6,840) | **−3.566** (−7,279) | −3.269 (−6,642) | −3.154 (−4,621) |
| hold, least, s100 / sn40 / f100 / fn40, ns | +0.193 / +0.141 / +0.135 / +0.095 | +0.205 / +0.206 / +0.137 / +0.091 | +0.247 / +0.161 / +0.101 / +0.060 | +0.163 / +0.192 / +0.096 / +0.076 |
| D-cache page r_a[31:12], worst s100 / −40 | −2.147 / −2.210 | −2.804 / −2.958 | −1.960 / −1.851 | −1.799 / −1.941 |
| D-cache request (d_idle_q / d_rdy_q / d_valid_q) | −2.789 / −2.716 | −3.429 / **−3.566** | −3.004 / −3.020 | −2.886 / −3.154 (from the D-cache's sb_a) |
| MEM's fields from EX | −2.414 / −2.354 | −3.223 / −3.390 | −2.600 / −2.721 | −1.623 / −1.637 |
| op_y (the operand forward's register) | −2.969 / −2.704 | −2.519 / −2.407 | −3.474 / −3.269 | −2.658 / −2.292 |
| synthesis: ppc_core ALUTs / registers | 17,372 / 10,518 | 17,382 / 10,518 | 17,392 / 10,550 | 17,447 / 10,542 |
| fit: ppc_core ALMs needed (memory ALMs) | 11,987.1 (340) | 11,727.1 (340) | 11,804.4 (340) | 11,851.2 (320) |
| fit: the whole design, ALM | 41,232 | 39,788 | 40,683 | 40,721 |

- **A's cost is timing.** Its worst at −40 °C is its own path, ex_s0ok through the incrementer into the D-cache's
  request registers, 0.31 ns worse than c125s_s1's worst. The compares' paths lose 0.65-0.85 ns into the D-cache and
  0.8-1.4 ns into MEM's fields. Area: +10 ALUTs at synthesis, no registers.
- **B's cost is area.** +32 registers and +20 ALUTs at synthesis (about 25-40 ALM). Its worst is within 0.015 ns of
  c125s_s1's at both slow corners. Its page path gets better (op_c sits beside the compares); the request paths lose
  0.2-0.3 ns and op_y's input 0.5 ns, as the operand forward now drives op_c's 32 registers too.
- The fit's ALM figures cannot measure either: five fits of near-identical RTL on the same seed span 39,788 to 41,232
  ALM, and their −40 °C worst −3.154 to −3.708 ns. One seed shows A's cost because A's worst path is A's own. It cannot
  rank B against B + S1 (c2fbs2_s1's better worst is the spread, not S1).

**6. A zero-cycle offset for B: S1** (§8.4, one copy per read port, here one copy fewer). mfsr / mfsrin had their own
16 x 32 copy of the segment registers (fsr_mem). They now read MEM's copy (dsr_mem). Its read address is MEM's sl_ea
while MEM's slow translation looks up (m.rp && !sl_done, from registers), and op_y[31:28] otherwise. In the lookup
cycles EX holds (mh_3), so a mfsr in EX never needs the port in a cycle that counts (checked). Benches: cpubench, `--alias`
and the seven translated profile sets at 3,000 seeds, identical to the base. Fit: ppc_core's memory ALMs 340 → 320
(fsr_mem's two MLABs), but synthesis +18 ALUTs (first form) and +55 (corrected) over B, while ppc_cpu moved +0 / +24:
synthesis itself moves tens of ALUTs across the hierarchy. Net between about −10 and +5 ALM, so it does not reliably
pay for B. Not taken: isr_mem / dsr_mem into M10K as R129 §5a did the TLB
ways (about −20 ALM each for +1 M10K each, and M10K is as binding: 534 / 553).

**7. The third way, priced on paper.** In the second word's cycle, detect the carry of 2 (ex_s0ok and op_x[11:0] +
op_y[11:0] + 4 ≥ 0x2000), make no request then (a term beside algn's in d_req), hold EX one cycle (a term in all three
copies of EX's hold), and on that edge fold the +4 into op_y itself, with a flag that takes it out of ea_x. The next
cycle's compares are two-operand.
- **Cycles:** one EX cycle per such access, in the rare case alone; none elsewhere.
- **Area:** B's incrementer, a third source into op_y's D (the operand forward's register, the critical family of
  R104 / R140) and the hold term: about B's area, on two critical paths instead of none.
- **Why not a cheaper retry:** a forced miss instead sends the second word to MEM, whose replay refetches, and the
  refetched instance meets the same carry (the livelock again). Avoiding that needs the replay without refetch for
  split words, which cpi3's RPX (R174) does not cover.
- It is no cheaper than B and slower than A or B in its case, so I did not build it.

*Wrong turns.*
- R183 said "a second compare against page − 1, or about +100 ALM". The second compare would have left the DBATs
  wrong. The +100 ALM was for duplicating the compare, not for moving the +4.
- My first base copy for the fits was `git archive` + `git apply` inside sm3-builds. git apply took the paths as the
  main repository's and applied nothing (csplit2's wrong turn too). Redone with `patch -p1`; its RTL then matched
  c125s_s1's rtl.md5 exactly.
- My first S1 gave MEM the segment-register port on `m.rp && !sl_done`, without m.valid. m.rp stays set in an empty MEM,
  so a mfsr in EX read a stale index. Its own check ("mfsr leaves EX while MEM looks up") stopped plain test_cpu,
  `--mode 2`, `--mode 1 --xpage` and every ppc_cpu run. It now uses mh_3's term, m.valid && m.rp && !sl_done. That
  fit (c2fbs_s1) was of the wrong RTL; its RBF is deleted and c2fbs2_s1 replaces it.
- I first read the fit's per-entity ALMs as the cost. They move by hundreds between fits of the same RTL; synthesis
  counts are the measure.

*Not done.* One seed per fit. No system bench. No board. Mine to choose (D-70).

**R187 — The SDRAM clocks from DDIO output registers, each clocked by its own PLL output set ahead of
clk_sys's 180 degrees, the SDRAM interfaces reported in every fit, and SU_PAIR. Board candidates, all with hold
positive at every corner (on the board since: c125ddpp_s1 passes, c130ddpp_s1 locks in VF3; 130 MHz variants below): dual 125 MHz `c125ddpp_s1` (RBF 5fe7b018, setup -3.11 / -3.06 ns), dual 130 MHz
`c130ddpp_s1` (RBF 2424ced6, -3.73 / -3.77), single 125 MHz `c125sd35_s1` (RBF 6ad6936f, -3.35 / -3.27). The
read capture stays at CL+2. Plain DDIO (clk_sys inverted, MemTest256's form) was built first and is reference
only: it puts the second SDRAM's read where 4000 ps put it, and 4000 ps fails on the board.**

Work in `sm3-builds/ddio/` (`tree`: worktree detached at 718e9e4 + `c125130-718e9e4.patch` + SU_PAIR + this entry's
changes, all in `ddio-718e9e4.patch`, md5 99698145; notes in `NOTES.md`). D-26, D-48, D-58, D-62, D-66, D-68, D-69,
D-71; R57 (Model 2's SDRAM constraints), R184 (c125130), R185 (r3dspeed). The tree takes this entry's changes at 130 MHz with (a)'s phases (section 9).

*What I believed:*
- The fault above 120 MHz since the module swap was the SDRAM interface. The clock pins were fed from a PLL output
  over the clock network and general routing, while their address, command and data leave from I/O-cell
  registers, and nothing constrained or reported that path difference. R184's c125dp35_s1, with outclk_2 moved
  0.5 ns earlier, runs every game.
- MemTest256's way would hold 180 degrees at any clock and fix the clock pin's path. That is a DDIO register clocked
  by the controller's clock, 0 in the high half and 1 in the low.
- With both clock pins on equal footing, one setting would suit both SDRAMs.

*What I know now:*

**1. SU_PAIR (D-71) went in from r3dspeed's diffs unchanged.** The RTL and generator diffs applied clean. The
bench's R3D_RESEED diff named r3dspeed's own paths, so it went in with `patch` on the file. The six files are
byte-identical to r3dspeed's tree, and gen_ucode.py regenerates the ROMs, the package and r3d_ucode.h byte for byte.
r3dspeed's Scud Race, Daytona 2 race and Sega Rally 2 dumps were deleted after its runs. So I reran the geometry
bench's model comparison on the two sets still here. VF3's 400 census frames (2,313,148 triangles) and Daytona 2's
attract, every 20th of d2scene's frames (676; 4,857,924 triangles), match the model on every triangle field with
the base tree's counts. Both logs are byte-identical to r3dspeed's SU_PAIR logs: geometry -2.64% and -2.96% on the
mean, no frame slower.

**2. The constraints.** Model3.sdc puts a generated clock on each SDRAM clock pin, sourced from the PLL output that
drives its DDIO. The fit report shows the pin clock's path: its global clock, the DDIO's `muxsel`, `dataout`, the
output buffer. Model 2's figures are in Model3.sdc too: input max 6.4 / min 1.0 ns, output max 1.5 / min -0.8 ns,
and the read multicycle. They apply only for TimeQuest, and only when `m3_sdram_io` is set before read_sdc.
fit.sh's `sdram_io.tcl` does that after every fit, once per capture edge, and writes `sdram_io.txt`. I kept them out
of the fitter and the flow's report on purpose. Every SDRAM register is in its I/O cell, so placement cannot move
these paths, but the fitter's automatic delay chains would chase figures whose read eye is shut on every
board-proven build, and that would move the board's capture point. In the flow's report, their read hold would also
stand among clk_sys's own paths.

I counted the read multicycle from m2_sdram. The READ leaves on edge 0 and the device drives the word tAC after its
second edge. dq_r samples at clk_sys edge CL + rd_lat_sel - 1, which is 3 T for CL+2. That gives setup multicycle 2
and no hold multicycle, since a burst changes the word every clock. Writes use the default relation.

**3. Plain DDIO first (wrong turn for this board).** `rtl/sys/m3_sdr_clk.sv` is MemTest256's altddio_out. With the
pins as clk_sys inverted, I took outclk_2 out of the PLL. Dual 125 `c125dd_s1`, dual 130 `c130dd_s2` (seed 1's hold
was -0.028 ns) and single `c125sd_s1` fitted. Their eyes were 1.6-2.1 ns wider than c125dp35's, because the pin
clock shared clk_sys's global clock with the registers it is timed against. Every write margin was positive, and the
two pins arrived within 0.05 ns of each other where outclk_2 had them 1.75 ns apart. But the second SDRAM's read
moved 0.47 ns later than on c125dp35 (setup -0.765 against -0.291 at slow 100 C). That is about where 4000 ps put
it, and on my board the dual SDRAM needs 3.5 ns at 125, not 4. These three are reference builds only,
not for the board.

**4. Phase-led DDIO.** The DDIO cells and constraints stayed. The pins now pass a PLL output through (`INV` 0)
instead of inverting clk_sys:
- One output for both pins, outclk_2 at 3500 ps (`c125dd35_s1`), put the first SDRAM inside c125dp35's ground on
  every figure, with its fast -40 C read hold at -2.042 against -2.094. The second SDRAM's slow 100 C setup was
  still -1.098. The pins' own global clock brings back TimeQuest's min / max spread, so the eye narrowed by 0.9 ns,
  and the nominal move was about 0.25-0.3 ns, not 0.5. Moving the shared clock earlier for the second SDRAM would
  take the first past -2.094 at once.
- So each pin has its own output: SDRAM_CLK on outclk_2 at 3500 ps, SDRAM2_CLK on outclk_3 at 3250 ps. 250 ps is
  one VCO step, and the most that keeps the second SDRAM's fast -40 C hold inside c125dp35's -2.233. At 130 MHz the
  leads are kept in time (3365 / 3125 ps, the PLL's 240 ps steps). The PLL refused 3346 ps: wrong turn below.
  pll_0002.v's outclk_2 is 3500 ps now, where the base patch had 4000.

DDIO pins moved 130 the right way but not far enough.
- **The old module.** VF3 did run at 130 before the module swap, on so130_s2. Its kept db, read with c125130's
  io3.tcl (the same figures), puts the first SDRAM's read centre at -1.64 ns at slow 100 C. That is 0.8 ns later
  than c130ddpp's -0.84 and 1.1 ns later than c125ddpp's -0.51. The old module took a later eye than the new one
  does. The figures compare builds on one module; they are not a pass mark.
- **The phases.** With c125ddpp_s1's centres as the target, c130ddpp needs both pin clocks 0.33 ns earlier. At 130
  the PLL steps are 240 ps, so one step each: outclk_2 3125 ps, outclk_3 2885 ps. That leaves each centre about
  0.1 ns late of c125ddpp's at slow 100 C. Fast -40 C read holds are -2.020 (first SDRAM) and -2.257 (second; 0.02
  past c125dp35's -2.233).
- **Writes.** Moving the clock earlier tightens them. At slow 100 C the first SDRAM is +0.027 / DQ -0.200 and the
  second -0.208 / -0.369, between c125ddpp's and c125dp35's.
- **Not taken.**
  - A finer VCO (120 ps steps at 1040 MHz) would only gain 0.06 ns, well inside the 0.2 ns the fits themselves
    move these figures, and needs hand-set PLL counters.
  - A falling-edge capture moves the capture by T / 2, which is too coarse.
  - An input delay chain on DQ delays the data, the wrong way for a setup-short eye.
- **The one capture change worth building:** dq_r clocked by its own PLL output a few hundred ps after clk_sys. It
  moves the reads later without touching the writes, and costs no cycle: cap still takes dq_r at the next clk_sys
  edge. Not built yet.
- **Fits**, both seed 1, hold positive at every corner:
  - (a) `c130ddpa_s1` (RBF 2629cdbc): both pins moved.
  - (b) `c130ddpb_s1` (RBF 280a590d): only the second SDRAM's moved.
  - Their core timing is c130ddpp's to the digit (same netlist, the phases touch only the pin clocks): -3.727 /
    -3.765 ns, hold +0.102 / +0.088 / +0.042 / +0.021. The I/O moved by exactly the step on each pin.
  - (a) goes on the board first. If VF3 runs, (b) says whether the first SDRAM needed the move. If (a) still locks,
    next is a second step or the capture clock. Both are for the board.

**8. (a) on the board, and the single build at 130.** c130ddpa_s1 runs VF3 through 20 minutes of attract and a full
round, and Scud Race and Daytona 2, with no lockup. Its fit is c130ddpp_s1's to the digit, so **the VF3 lockup at
130 was the SDRAM read timing, not a clk_sys path**.

Frame rates on (a):
- Sega Rally 2: mostly 30 in game, 60 in attract.
- Scud Race: small drops to 30.
- Daytona 2: 60 in attract, mostly 30 on track 1.

I fitted the single build at (a)'s first-SDRAM phase: `c130sd_s1` (RBF ade245af), outclk_2 3125 ps.
- Setup -3.463 / -3.630 ns; hold +0.242 / +0.202 / +0.098 / +0.078.
- Its read sits within 0.15 ns of (a)'s first SDRAM: -1.053 / -0.154 at slow 100 C, hold -2.118 at fast -40 C.
- That is 1.2 ns earlier in centre than so130_s2, the pre-swap build that ran VF3 on the old module, with 0.68 ns
  less fast-corner hold. No old-module build I have figures for sat this early. If one fixed phase does not cover
  both modules, the old module will fail on hold, not on setup. It goes on the old module to find out.

**9. (b) on the board, and what goes in.** c130ddpb_s1 (3365 / 2885 ps, only the second SDRAM moved) also runs
VF3 with no lockup. With c130ddpp_s1 (3365 / 3125) locking, the failure at 130 was the second SDRAM's read; the
first SDRAM runs at 3365 or 3125 on these chips. I keep (a)'s 3125 for the first SDRAM all the same: its eye centre
(-0.60 at slow 100 C) is nearer c125ddpp's (-0.51) than 3365's (-0.84), which is the margin other chips will need.
The tree goes in at 130 MHz with outclk_2 3125 and outclk_3 2885 ps, c130ddpa_s1's settings (the dual build and
M3_RELEASE are the qsf's two switches). The old single module waits until I next open the board (D-73), so the
single build's 3125 ps is proven only on the new modules. With the 130 MHz clock, m3_frame_busy's frame constant
passed 2^31 in its int arithmetic (debug builds only; release builds leave the block out); it is now taken as
x * 278 + x * 144 / 1000, the same figure at every clock.

**1. The race cannot be benched; the transfer disagrees with the board.** The system bench reaches Daytona 2's game

(R185), and Sega Rally 2 in game 40-50 h with a coin script. R171's frame-1300 checkpoint cannot be carried into the

30 on track 1" on c130ddpa_s1, and R159 showed Daytona 2 has no governor (each loop is one vblank or two). So the
transfer is at least 5-8% optimistic on the race. If the board's p50 is 1.00-1.05, -3.13% takes it to 0.97-1.02:
some loops flip, most stay at 30. p90 sits about 7% above p50, so a race held at 60 needs about -8% to -12% of the
CPU's work at 130.

**6. The board's first reading, and the fix (2026-11-17).**
- **What cfb_s1 showed.**
  - Sega Rally 2 counted properly. Racing at 57-58 fps, every frame was under 0.9 vblank. The start line read
    1.25-1.61. Slowdowns with cars or the audience in view read 2.00-2.06 for both min and max.
  - Daytona 2's race counted nothing (row 7 FFFF0000 00000000 00000100 3032A27C every second). Its FPS counter read
    27-32, mostly 28-29 at 57.5 Hz, so nearly every race loop missed.
- **The cause: R104's Daytona 2 rule waited for the 0x100030 vblank poll (4C6CC), which only the boot runs.** The
  game loop is paced by the decrementer, as R159 / R160 have it:
  - the vblank handler 1D74 reloads DEC, which fires 0.88 vblank later;
  - 1C44 counts 0x100033;
  - 4C6FC waits in 4C73C-4C744 while DEC is negative, then in 4C754-4C760 for the count;
  - the loop starts at 4C764.
  - In Supermodel's race (idle skip off) 4C6CC never runs, and in the bench's attract the module counted nothing
    either. My first bench check had only boot frames.
- **The fix.** For Daytona 2 a frame now runs from the exit at 4C764, counted from 0 there, to the first entry into
  either wait: the study's "CPU reaches 4C6FC, deadline 1.000". The boot's poll keeps its rule.
  - Supermodel's race replayed through the rule: 2,199 frames for 2,200 loops, each equal to the census's work for
    its frame.
  - The bench's attract 1301-1316, the RTL driven at the bench's clock events: 14 of 14 frames equal the replay to
    the unit, 0.884 vblank. The old rule gives 0 frames.
- **D's stuck 0x227C** was the last frame counted in the boot (1.0001 vblank), held since.
- **VF3 is broken in the same way at "SEGA presents".** Its pacing branches over its vblank poll straight into a
  decrementer wait whose first word is also the poll's exit, so the module sees exits and no entries. Not fixed here;
  VF3 holds 60.
- **Sega Rally 2's 2.0 frames, from the code.**
  - Apart from the pacing poll and the delay loop, the game can wait only in its Real3D DMA calls: 6F468 and 6F50C,
    165 a frame, polling C200000C bit 7.
  - The frame's 0x88000000 flush goes through them too.
  - It reads no Real3D or tile-generator status.
  - So a frame pinned at 2.0 with min = max is the 3D side holding the DMA (r3d_cmd's swap wait is the likely
    cause), not CPU work.
- **The split.** The module now also counts each frame's ticks spent in the games' DMA waits (VF3 61DC4-61DD0,
  Daytona 2 2B64-2B7C and 52A4-52C4, Sega Rally 2 its two DMA calls).
  - It shows them on row 6 and as row 7's last value: the longest frame's {DMA wait, rest}. Rows 0-5 are off in this
    build.
  - The four-value form needed 4,227 LABs of 4,191 (`cfb2_s1` did not fit). The trimmed form fits as `cfb3_s1`:
    setup -3.807 / -3.837, hold +0.250 / +0.191 / +0.099 / +0.072, SDRAM I/O c130ddpa_s1's.
  - RBF 15fab5a4, md5 15fab5a491aefe9722851a003e34d9c4.
- **Daytona 2's attract on the board's tree at 130 dual (the overnight runs).**
  - Base: loop to 4C6FC p50 0.850, p90 0.879 over frames 1000-1300; 0.884 at 1301-1316, of which the DMA is 0.027.
  - With the items: 0.820 / 0.848; 0.851 at 1301-1316, -3.2% to -3.7%.
  - Against R171's 0.940 at 120 single (0.868 by the clock) the dual memory gives Daytona 2 about nothing here.
- **Another wrong turn: the OOM.** The post-processing read VF3's 3.5 GB event log into memory with no cap, and the
  OOM killer took VS Code at 09:57. Analyses now stream and run under the 7 GB cap.

*On the board (2026-11-17).* cfb3_s1 (15fab5a4, the fixed measurement) read once a second over a lap of Daytona 2's
track 1: FPS 27-31, every race frame 1.01-1.10 vblank (peaks 1.24-1.31 around three corners), DMA wait 0.03-0.04
of it. So the race misses its 1.000 deadline by 1-10%; the items' 3.2-3.7% moves only the shortest frames under.
Holding 60 through the lap needs about -10% of the race frame, about -25% at the worst spots. "The rest" is not
all instruction time: cache misses, SDRAM waits and held Real3D accesses are in it, and SR2 (R189) showed how much a
held Real3D access can be. The items stay out of the tree until that split is measured; m3_frame_busy and its
release-build switch (M3_FBUSY_BUILD, commented out in the qsf) go in.

**R189 — Sega Rally 2's 30 fps at the start line and in crowded views is r3d_mem's run FIFO, not the DMA's
speed: its 393 ten-word 8E moves a frame make about 270 deferred runs, the 256-entry FIFO fills while the geometry
reads bank R, and r3d_mem takes nothing more until the geometry ends. Reproduced on a bench with the RTL write path
(DMA wait 0.59-0.68 vblank a frame, frames 1.29-1.38, 27.6 fps; the board's cfb3_s1 0.61-0.81 and 1.29-1.79). Three
small changes in r3d_mem fix it: 0.11-0.14 vblank, frames 0.82-0.84, 60 fps on the bench, no case slower.
The same bench found a second bug in the same block: the 8E group drops a word when one arrives in the clock its age
runs out. Desk and bench only; nothing fitted, nothing on the board.**

Work in `sm3-builds/sr2dma/` (`tree`: `git archive ae56d77`, the board's 130 MHz dual tree; the fix in
`fix/rtl/real3d/r3d_mem.sv`; my Supermodel copy with a Real3D write census in `sm/`; the bench in `sim/`; notes in
`NOTES.md`). D-48, D-57, D-58; R100 (the Step 2 DMA device on m3_scripts), R112 / R114 (R3P and the MPC105's
ordering), R144 and R156 (the posted-write FIFO, the 8E group), R162 (ddrload's DDR3 path checks), R168 (Sega Rally
2), R185 (r3dspeed's SR2 frames), R188 (cpuspeed's frame-busy build, cfb3_s1).

*What I believed:*
- From cfb3_s1's rows 6 and 7 (R188): SR2's CPU work is 0.57-0.82 vblank everywhere, and its slow frames are DMA wait,
  0.6-0.8 vblank a frame at the start line and in the crowd. So the DMA, or the Real3D behind it, was slow per word:
  r3d_cmd's 32-entry posted-write FIFO full behind r3d_mem's drain (polygon RAM as one-word DDR3 writes, two copies,
  through the DDR3 arbiter's turn), or sw_wait holding h_rdy at the flip.
- The isolated 2.0-vblank frames, whose time is outside the DMA polls, were a Real3D store held by h_rdy.

*What I know now:*

**1. What SR2 writes (my Supermodel copy, srally2, -no-idle-skip, the cpuspeed play script).** I added `M3DMALOG`:
per frame the Real3D words the CPU and the DMA write, by window; in a frame window every DMA with its instruction
position in the frame, and the tile generator's 00 / 08 / 0C writes. The CPU writes nothing to the Real3D itself;
everything is DMA from work RAM.

| Supermodel frames | 8E words | polygon RAM words | DMAs a frame |
|---|---|---|---|
| attract (1000-1500) | 4,600-6,050 | 9,420-10,610 | ~200 |
| start line (5520-5820) | 7,360-9,030 | 6,272 | 393-428 (393 to 8E) |
| Desert race (6000-6030) | ~6,100-6,500 | 998 | 270-351 (224 ten-word 8E) |

At the start line 393 of the 405 DMAs go to 8E, most of them ten words (8E014028, 8E014050, ... from 6D714 and
6D668), with eleven polygon RAM moves of 424-896 words and one 88. The texture port gets three words a frame only in
the start line's first 33 frames; no 94 in the race. The flip is at line 368 (tile register 08 = 0x170, once at boot).

**2. The mechanism.** With M3_R3B, r3d_mem gathers 8E words in an aligned four-word group, flushed when full, when a
write for another group comes, or after six clocks with none (R156). While the geometry reads bank R, the group's R
copy is deferred as a run: it extends the open run if it starts at the run's end; otherwise the open run goes into the
256-entry run FIFO and a new one opens. Runs are copied only while the geometry is not reading R, and with the FIFO
full `w_ready` is low. SR2's ten-word moves: words 500A-5013, 5014-501D, 501E-5027, ... Every other move starts in the
group the last one ended in (501C: 1C-1D, then 1E-1F), and between the moves that group ages out. Its second visit
starts inside the open run, not at its end, so it closes the run and opens a new one: about 270 runs a frame. The
geometry reads bank R from the flip for 0.54-0.67 vblank. The run FIFO fills partway through the frame's 8E moves,
and from then until the geometry ends r3d_mem takes nothing. r3d_cmd's FIFO and R3P fill, the DMA engine waits on
the bus, and the CPU waits in 6F4B0's poll, whose load (R114) waits in B_DEC for R3P to empty.

**3. The bench, `sr2path` (`sim/sr2path_tb.sv`, `tb_sr2path.cpp`).** r3d_cmd, r3d_mem, m2_sdram, m3_ddr_arb (eight
ports) and m3_ddr3p are the RTL, built as the board is (M3_DMAFAST, M3_R3B). In C++: SR2's frame-5600 DMA list at its
census positions, scaled to 0.70 vblank of CPU work; the call as the game's (poll, three register writes, poll, each
behind R114); m3_scripts' move (16-word FIFO, writes first, line reads 70 clocks as R144's 41 + 29, single reads 45, R3P
beats 2 clocks); the pacing poll (a frame that ends after the next vblank waits for the one after); the flip at line
368; the vblank interrupt (four status / I/O accesses, each behind R114). The other traffic per drawn frame comes from
r3dspeed's SR2 start-line figures: store writes 923 KB, reads 1.84 MB, layer 762 KB, 30,165 texture fills, replay
1.32 M clocks, geometry 1.52 M clocks. The geometry's polygon RAM and VROM reads use Scud Race's rates (2,691 / 5,442).
Scan-out and sound run throughout, and the DDR3 uses ddrload's HPS profiles. At every swap the bench checks that both
copies of every 8E and polygon RAM word hold the last value written (nothing is deferred at a swap). With no other
traffic it moves a long DMA at 13.3-14.8 clocks a word, R144's 14.9.

| frame 5600 (start line), 12 vblanks, seeds 1-3 | DMA wait / frame | frame | fps | run FIFO full | runs / frame | swap check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base RTL, no other traffic | 0.568 | 1.268 | 27-29 | 21% of the time | 273 | |
| base RTL, start-line traffic, DDR3 `base` | 0.588 | 1.288 | 27.6 | 21.6% | 275 | 1 of 3 runs FAIL |
| base RTL, start-line traffic, `hps1` | 0.676-0.678 | 1.376-1.378 | 27.6 | 21.6% | 275 | 1 of 3 FAIL |
| board, cfb3_s1, start line | 0.61-0.81 | 1.29-1.79 | 28-29 | | | |
| fixed (section 5), `base`, seeds 1-3 | 0.114 | 0.815 | 60 | 0 | 33 | PASS |
| fixed (section 5), `hps1`, seeds 1-3 | 0.139 | 0.840 | 60 | 0 | 33 | PASS |

The wait is there with no other DDR3 traffic at all, so neither the drain rate, the arbiter nor the texture path
causes it. They add 0.02-0.11 vblank on top. The drain is the run FIFO, and nothing else. sw_wait held h_rdy for one
clock at every swap: nothing is pending at the flip, because the geometry has long finished by then and the copies
are done.

**4. The second bug: the 8E group drops a word.** The swap check failed on the base RTL in 2 of 6 runs (2 and 4
words) and never with the fix. I traced one (word 05BF2): it was pushed into r3d_cmd, and every burst after it masked
its lanes in both copies, which kept the previous frame's value. `g_flush` includes `g_age == G_AGE`, and `w_ready`
takes a hit for the open group (`!g_v || g_hit`) without looking at the flush. A hit offered in the clock the age runs
out is acknowledged (r3d_cmd pops it), and the same clock goes to S_GW without it (`g_we` has `!g_flush`). It needs the
next word of a group exactly six clocks after the last. SR2's single-word 8E writes (its moves are not line-aligned)
give that now and then; Scud Race's trace (below) never did. On the board it would be a
culling RAM word one frame stale. That is not established as visible, but it is wrong either way.

**5. The fix (`fix2/rtl/real3d/r3d_mem.sv`, all under M3_R3B).**
- A group whose words are already in the open run needs no run of its own. The copy reads W, which has the new words,
  and copies the whole run. `g_same` is set as a group opens: it is the group just flushed (`g_grp` still holds that
  group, and the compare is g_hit's). `o_lgv` is set when a group goes into the open run as its last, and cleared by a
  one-word run or a group written straight to R. `x_in = x_g && o_v && o_lgv && g_same` leaves the runs as they are,
  and rf_push excludes it.
- The age flush only when no hit is offered: `(g_age == G_AGE && !g_hit)`, which is the rule the comment already states
  ("or when no write is waiting").
- A copy pauses for a waiting write. *Wrong turn:* with the first two changes alone, race frame 6000 got slower,
  DMA wait 0.063 -> 0.073 vblank, though still at 60. S_CP copies a whole run before it goes back to S_IDLE, and the
  merged ten-word stream is one run of about 2,240 words, so its copy held every write for tens of thousands of
  clocks (base's runs of about 20 words let the writes in between). Now the copy has its own position `pa`, `cp_v`
  marks a copy begun, and between pieces (a pair of 8E words, or a polygon RAM burst) S_CP returns to S_IDLE if a
  write waits and the run FIFO is not full. S_IDLE resumes the copy when none waits. `pending` includes cp_v, so the
  swap waits for it and writes defer, as during any copy. A write into the paused range is copied again by its own run.

| bench, 12 vblanks, hps1 unless noted | base: DMA, frame | first two changes | all three (fix2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| start line 5600, DDR3 `base` | 0.587, 1.289 | 0.139, 0.839 | 0.114, 0.815 |
| start line 5600 | 0.673, 1.375 | 0.173, 0.874 | 0.139, 0.840 |
| race 6000 (224 ten-word 8E moves, CPU 0.62) | 0.063, 0.684 | 0.073, 0.694 | 0.062, 0.683 |
| race 6030 (351 DMAs) | 0.229, 0.850 | 0.093, 0.713 | 0.078, 0.699 |
| Daytona 2 attract 1305 (my census, CPU 0.85) | 0.091, 0.942 | 0.091, 0.942 | 0.091, 0.942 |
| run FIFO full | 11-22% of the time | 0 | 0 |
| swap check | 2 of 8 runs FAIL | PASS | PASS |

Race 6030 on base (DMA 0.229, frame 0.85) sits inside the board's racing figures (DMA 0.08-0.35, frames 0.6-0.9).
Heavier views have more ten-word moves, so the run FIFO fills earlier; that is the car and crowd slowdowns. fix2 is
never slower than base in any case I ran. sw_wait held h_rdy one clock at every swap, base and fix alike.

Scud Race's 10,770-frame trace through ddrload's host bench (R162's check, 141 draws against Supermodel's dumps):
base and the first two changes give identical logs (3,753,600,132 cycles, 28,470 runs, 59,735 copy transfers, 0 words
differ). fix2 gives the same again, to the cycle. So on Scud Race's DMA none of the three changes ever acts.

Cost, Quartus 17 map of r3d_mem alone (AW 26, M3_R3B, virtual pins): the first two changes 594 ALMs needed and 582
ALUTs, the same as base, +2 registers, M10K unchanged (2). A first form that kept the open run's last group in an
18-bit register cost +14 ALM. The resumable copy's own 21-bit position brings fix2 to 603 ALMs needed (+9), 593 ALUTs (+11), 281
registers (+21), M10K unchanged. `--analyze_file` of fix2's r3d_mem: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

D-58: every word is still written to both copies, and every deferred word is copied before the swap. The swap check
passes on every run.

**6. The isolated 2.0-vblank frames: not reproduced.** In every bench run the vblank handler's longest hold is
0.001-0.002 vblank, at CPU work 0.70, 0.80 and 0.90 alike. The vblank comes at the frame's start, and the stall runs
from the flip (line 368) to the geometry's end, so the two never overlap in steady running. The likely form is
desk-only: an interrupt taken inside a stalled DMA call. Its status and I/O accesses then wait behind R3P (R114) while
the DMA engine holds the bus waiting for room, and that time retires in the handler, so the module counts it as
"rest". It needs the same stall the fix removes, but it stays a hypothesis until a board build shows the 2.0 frames
gone.

**7. What the reference says about the real board's DMA and Real3D write rate.** Nothing in the study, Supermodel or
MAME times it. Supermodel's DMACopy and MAME's real3d_dma move the whole block at the length write, so "instant" is
an emulator convenience, not a measurement. The bounds I have are R144's. The PCI is 33 MHz and 32 bits, at most
132 MB/s; a bursting master's memory-to-memory move tops out near 55 MB/s. The Step 2.x DMA device (0x178611DB) has
no datasheet I can find. At 55 MB/s, SR2's 57.7 KB start-line frame would take about 1.05 ms, 0.06 vblank; at
132 MB/s about 0.025. Our fixed path inside the calls is 21-26 clocks a word at 130 MHz, 20-25 MB/s, so 0.14-0.17
vblank with 405 calls' overhead. That is slower than any bursting PCI master, but inside SR2's frame. Unknown: whether
the real Real3D ever holds a DMA (its update buffers, whose sizes the 9C registers set, have no documented behaviour
when full), and the real device's per-call overhead.

and r3d_recip, byte-identical to snap/b6items's, without the CPI items), plus section 5's r3d_mem.

*On the board (2026-11-19).* `cd74_s1` (743bfb4c: this fix, b6 and R190's area, with the frame-busy rows; dual,
130 MHz, 3125 / 2885 ps). VF3, Scud Race and Daytona 2 run with no lockup. Over a full lap of Sega Rally 2 the
longest frame's DMA wait is 0.00-0.22 vblank everywhere, against 0.61-0.81 on cfb3_s1, and most of the lap holds
57-58 fps where cfb3_s1 had three long stretches at 28-29. Three slow spots remain, and they are not this fault:
- At the start line (29-30 s) every frame is exactly 2.00 vblank with 0.13 of DMA wait and 1.87 held elsewhere.
- In two stretches (56-62 s and 92-95 s) every frame the CPU runs is under one vblank (0.88-0.95 at most) while the
  FPS counter reads 19-43: the game loop runs at 60 and the Real3D drops frames. r3d_cmd drops a frame when the
  previous draw is still running at the flip, and does not hold the host then.
- At 60 s, frames near 2.0 with the host held, as at the start line. The likely hold is sw_wait waiting for
  m_can_swap, which waits for r3d_mem's deferred copy, which waits for the geometry to stop reading.
All three are the Real3D's own speed in heavy views (geometry, rasteriser or texture path, not yet split), which
the sr2path bench could not show: its geometry and rasteriser are stand-ins. The isolated 2.0 frames of the first
board run were this kind, not an interrupt inside a stalled DMA call as I first guessed.

**R190 — D-74's third item: a zero-cycle, ALM-only pass on the 130 MHz dual-SDRAM tree (ae56d77). The room
was the second SDRAM: it carries the first SDRAM's general controller and port for traffic that is only ever the
CPU's work RAM, on its second chip, in word form. Told so at compile time it loses 146 ALUTs and 125 registers in
the fit. With the edge walker at 54 bits and the FP divider's remainder at 54 (area4's priced rows 1 and 2) and the
DDR3 arbiter's fields as an AND-OR (row 4), the five changed blocks give −131 ALMs needed and −127 placed by entity,
−220 ALUTs, −181 registers, for no M10K, no DSP and no MLAB, and every bench is identical to the base, clock for
clock. The fit (`ar130_s1`) is 0.06 / 0.26 ns better on worst setup and 12% / 10% on TNS than c130ddpa_s1, hold
positive at every corner. The LAB count barely moves (4,190 -> 4,189): the fitter spreads, as R179 found.**

*What I believed:*

**4. Tried and not kept.**
- **m2_sdram's request latches without their reset (N).** Their values are never read before the clock their pend
  rises (random-start runs identical), and the controllers lost 23 and 40 ALUTs, but both m3_sdr_ports grew 37-41
  ALUTs each, +56 in the whole map. N2 (the address latch keeping its clear) the same, +11 in those blocks: the
  growth is on the ports' column data side (p_din / p_be from col16). Why Quartus does better with the clear I have
  not established. Not kept.
- **The probe's writes through port 0**, so the second controller's dedicated write port could be tied off: that
  port costs 24 ALUTs and 28 registers there (priced with a broken probe), and a working probe needs a 16-bit select
  on c_din and an 18-bit one on wb_din / wb_be (the column data path, R107's worst once), or a 32-bit select on the
  port's s_wdata. About even. Not built.
- **The second SDRAM's OSD-message counter (29 bits) from the one-second tick**: that counter is held in the game's
  reset, which is where a missing module holds the game. Not built.
- **The first SDRAM's 77 µs bring-up made the second's 110 µs**, so Quartus could merge the two init counters: a
  power-up change for about 10 ALM. Not built.
- **Telemetry counters** (m3_bus's n_*, r3d_rast's n_pix / f_cycles, the VPU's issue counts): already gone in a
  release (unconnected, removed by map).

- I chained a map on `ps | grep '[g]ate.sh'`, which matched its own command line, and the N2 map never started.
- My expected value for one DCHIP1 constant-fold case was wrong (101 for 110); Quartus was right.
- A `git apply --check` with no file waited on its input; nothing was changed (the main checkout's status is as it was).

parameters at 130 MHz: r3d_cmd (M3_DMAFAST, M3_R3B), r3d_mem, r3d_texup (the Step 2 port as M3_STEP2_TEX builds it),
r3d_geo (SETUP_OUT, LOD_WORD) and its three readers, r3d_rast (MIP, RUNO), m3_ddr_arb, m3_ddr3p (PIPE, MAXQ 8) and
m2_sdram, with the DDR3's HPS model (hps1) and the SDRAM at its pins. Memory comes from one Supermodel dump; every
write the frame makes carries the dump's own value, so each frame draws the same scene and a run is the scene's
steady state, with the real write traffic, deferred copies and swap waits. The host is sr2path's (DMA engine, R3P,
R114, the vblank interrupt) with the 0C write behind R114 too, and two pacings: the vblank poll (Sega Rally 2) and
Daytona 2's decrementer event, 0.885 vblank after the vblank. It runs at about 360 kHz, a scene in under a minute.
- Census and dumps come from one Supermodel run per game (two runs of one script part at boot, R185), with a
  census line I added for the Step 2 texture port's words (my Supermodel copy; sr2dma's sources).
- **Daytona 2 does not wait out its DMAs.** Its code (cpi's race disassembly) builds a list of {source,
  destination, length} at 0x711000 and starts the first (2830 / 2A34); the DMA-end interrupt (1A40 -> 2BA4) starts
  each next one (2CF8); 5284 polls 0x700100 (the frame-busy module's 52A4-52C4) only before the next list. With
  sr2path's call model the bench's DMA wait was 0.12-0.22 vblank against the board's 0.03-0.04; with the list model
  0.04-0.08. All its DMAs sit in the loop's last third (positions 0.66-1.0).
- Flips: Daytona 2's tile register 08 is 0x14F (line 335), 0.999 vblank after the decrementer event, so its loop's
  1.000 deadline is also the flip's. Sega Rally 2's line 368 is 0.962 vblank after its release: a frame of 0.97-1.0
  still makes 60 Hz, a flip late.

- **Daytona 2: the held part of its frame is 0.005-0.007 vblank** (the frame less its DMA wait less the CPU's work;
  median 0.0067, at most 0.013 over the 24 race frames): the DMA-end interrupt handlers' own time (0.005, of it
  R114's wait for R3P 0.0001-0.002) and the vblank interrupt (0.001). The swap never waits
  (its writes come after its geometry has ended; copies 0.00003). So of the board's 1.01-1.10, about 0.5% is the
  Real3D holding the CPU; the DMA wait the module already splits out (0.03-0.04 on the board, 0.04-0.08 here) is the
  polygon RAM list's one-word DDR3 writes (r3d_mem S_DW, about 25 clocks a word, r3d_cmd's FIFO full 5% of the
  time). The rest is the CPU's work, as R188 had it. Bus contention between the CPU's misses and the DMA engine is
  not in this bench (the CPU is not RTL); R188's system bench has it inside its "CPU" figure.
- **Sega Rally 2's start line on the bench is CPU + DMA at the deadline** (0.94-1.09), with the Real3D adding
  0.00-0.09 through late swaps: the geometry ends near the flip, the copies of everything written while it read
  bank R take 0.11-0.15 more, and the swap waits for them while the DMA calls are held. The board's frames of
  exactly 2.00 (DMA 0.13, rest 1.87) are not reproduced. Ruled out on the bench: the run FIFO (never full), the
  Step 2 texture uploads (one a frame from 5391 to 5552, 32x32 to 512x128: their VROM copy holds only their own
  words), sw_wait beyond the copies, r3d_cmd's FIFO full outside the calls. With Sega Rally 2's cost per instruction
  from the board's racing rest (about 1.63e-6, 11% above Daytona 2's) the start line's CPU work is 0.90-0.95: still
  under 1.87.
- **Sega Rally 2's pack-in-view frames are the geometry's**, and a third of its time there is the rasteriser's
  store refusing records: while refused, the store is in W_WR (a record's 11-beat DDR3 write, through a port it
  shares with the replay's reads) 67-81% and W_RUN (a run-list entry's write) 13-24%. A measurement-only store that
  never refuses puts SR2 5600's geometry at 0.72 against 0.85 (optimistic: it also removes the store's DDR3
  traffic). Other attract views are the replay's (0.84-1.00), where the Z band refusing pairs (43-56% of the
  replay) and the texture cache refusing pixels (12-53%) lead, as R160 / R185 found.
- The scripted Desert race never meets the board's crowd / car slowdowns (full throttle and centre steer leave the
  pack); the attract's demo races are the stand-in.

**3. Built** (each against eccf1a0; patches in `sm3-builds/r3d75/patches/`):
- **v5, the store posts its writes** (`r3d_rast_store.sv`): the intake takes a record while earlier ones are being
  placed and written. Eight record slots in the record buffer's M10Ks (128 of their 256 words; they used 16); a hold
  carries a complete record's registered fit to the back end; the back end places the record's {address, beats}
  for an in-order writer and its closed runs in an eight-entry queue (MLAB), and goes on to the bands; the writer and
  the queue share the store's port with the replay. The fit's read of the list pointers comes at least two clocks
  after every earlier record's W_ADDR (from word H + 5 the intake waits while one is held or placing); w_ready is
  registers only. The bank is full only when the slots and the queue are empty.
- **v3, 8E copies by four-word group** (`r3d_mem.sv`, `m3_system.sv`'s `s_lo`): one eight-column read (m2_sdram's
  p_long on a WB port; the first four columns kept from s_lo) and one eight-column write, where a pair took a read
  and two writes (77% of the copy window was those). W and R are equal outside the pending runs, so the group's
  other words copy as they are, as the pair's did.

| loop bench, hps1 | base | v5 | v3 | v5 + v3 |

| SR2 5600: frame mean / max | 1.004 / 1.054 | 0.979 / 0.982 | 0.976 / 0.979 | 0.980 / 0.989 |
| SR2 5600: geometry (refused) / copies / swap wait | 0.846 (0.27) / 0.151 / 0.023 | 0.802 (0.09) / 0.135 / 0.002 | 0.848 / 0.066 / 0 | 0.803 (0.09) / 0.071 / 0 |
| SR2 attract 1400 / 1450 / 1500 / 1550: geometry | 0.997 / 0.977 / 0.919 / 0.969 | 0.981 / 0.930 / 0.955 / 0.924 | 0.999 / 0.989 / 0.922 / 0.977 | 0.978 / 0.934 / 0.965 / 0.925 |
| the same: fps | 43.1 each | 43.1 / 57.5 / 43.1 / 57.5 | 43.1 each | 43.1 / 57.5 / 43.1 / 57.5 |
| Daytona 2 5000: frame / geometry | 1.079 / 0.721 | 1.081 / 0.706 | 1.079 / 0.721 | 1.081 / 0.706 |

On nine light frames (SR2 race 6040 / 6440 / 7000, attract 1000 / 1250 / 1650 / 1900 / 2100 / 3000) v5 + v3 is

0.674 -> 0.713 (0.114 -> 0.153); v3 alone is the base's there (0.689 / 0.673). These frames move about 10,000

  garden) and the geometry at 6600 (1.04, the crash camera), as R185 had them; the store side changes neither
  much (v5: 0.721 -> 0.706 at 5000).

*Proof:*
- Whole-rasteriser bench (MIP), VF3's and Daytona 2's 400 census frames, base against v5: 0 pixels wrong in all
  800, shaded pixels identical (145,366,386 / 131,975,872), 0 port-rule violations; binning 153.66 M -> 79.12 M
  clocks (-48.5%, lower in 400 of 400) and 139.25 M -> 67.24 M (-51.7%, lower in 365, the rest equal); replay
  within +-915 clocks a frame (0.04% of a vblank; the replay overlaps the next frame's binning on the bench's
  memory, so it moves both ways, net -0.00% / +0.00%). The first form (v1, a two-record overlap) gave 0 wrong too.
- sr2path (R189's bench, its swap check: both copies of every 8E and polygon RAM word written hold its last value at
  every swap), base against v3, SR2 5600 / 6000 / 6030 and Daytona 2's race frames, hps1, seeds 1-3: 12 of 12 PASS;
  copy transfers 40,584 -> 20,328 (5600); frames equal to the clock's rounding or shorter, none longer.
- Verilator assertions live in every run: the store's fit, bands and list pointers registered a cycle early (now
  checked at T1), the slots' ring (ip == wp + nsl), r3d_mem's held s_dout during the copy's write.
- `quartus_map --analyze_file` (17.0): v5's r3d_rast_store, v3's r3d_mem and m3_system, 0 errors, 0 warnings.

Where the area would come from (zero-cycle, D-48): none is found in this work. The chip is at 41,076 / 41,910 ALM and
4,188 / 4,191 LABs, so even v3 (+80 by map) needs a pass like R190's, and v5 with the polygon RAM gathering
(about +160-200 more) a larger one. Candidates priced before and not taken: R188's three output-registered MLABs
into M10K (10-20 ALM each for 3 of the 17 free M10K), R190's bring-up counters merged (about 10). Together they
roughly pay for v3, not for the rest.

*Measurement for the board (`meas/`, not fitted):* overlay row 6's first value in the frame-busy build becomes the
Real3D's second: {frames dropped at the flip, swaps, the longest swap wait in units of 256 clocks}, in place of the
DMA wait's {min, max} (no longer read, so not built). r3d_cmd gets an `o_swait` output; m3_system a drop pulse.
Unit bench PASS; lint the base's 11 warnings; `--analyze_file` 0 / 0 (fb_dual). m3_frame_busy alone 416 -> 481 ALMs
needed with the new value; net of E's removal about +20-30 (desk).

*Wrong turns:*
- My first bench dropped the Step 2 texture port's words, as m3_system does without M3_STEP2_TEX; the board build
  has it on. The census then needed the port's words, which only a Supermodel line of mine gives.
- My first Daytona 2 model waited out every DMA, as Sega Rally 2's code does: three to five times the board's DMA
  wait. Its code runs lists from the DMA-end interrupt.
- The first Daytona 2 Supermodel run had no loop log, and a DMA cannot be placed in the loop without it.
- v1 (overlap one record) and v2 (record writes first on the store's port) each moved the geometry 1-3%: the back
  end's own DDR3 writes were the limit, not the intake; v4 posted the records and then the run-list writes were the
  limit, which v5 posts too.
- A launcher of mine waited on `pgrep -f` of a pattern that matched its own command line; it never started.

**Addendum (2026-11-20): polygon RAM bursts, v5 decided, the measurement build `cr3m_s1`.**
- **Polygon RAM bursts** (`vb`, on v3; `patches/vb-eccf1a0.patch`): r3d_mem gathers 98 words as it does 8E's: an
  aligned four-word group (two DDR3 beats), one two-beat burst to W and then to R (or a deferred four-word run),
  where each word had been two one-beat writes. The group's words sit in two MLAB arrays by parity so a beat's two
  words read together; d_be is the beat's two lanes from the group's mask. Map: 683 -> 718 ALMs needed over v3
  (603 base), 2 M10K, 256 MLAB bits; `--analyze_file` 0 / 0.
- *Checks.* sr2path's swap check, base against vb, SR2 5600 / 6000 / 6030 and the SR2 attract 1000 / 1900, Daytona
  2's race and attract, VF3, seeds 1-3: 24 of 24 PASS, every case equal or shorter (Daytona 2's race frames 1.24 ->
  1.08 there, SR2 5600 0.840 -> 0.817). Scud Race's trace (ddrload's host bench, hps1): 87 draws, 87 geometry ends,
  textures twice and 209 8C images, 0 words differ; the trace runs to its end in 2.78 G clocks against 4.63 G.
  The loop bench (new census, 27 frames): no frame slower than base; SR2 attract DMA 0.105-0.175 -> 0.102-0.131,
  frames -0.002 to -0.047 (1400 43.1 -> 57.5 fps); SR2 5700 1.334 -> 1.286; Daytona 2's list wait 0.047-0.170 ->
  0.038-0.061 (the board's is already 0.03-0.04, so there about -0.01 to -0.02, desk). v3 alone showed +0.002 / +0.003
  in two attract frames; with the bursts every frame is shorter.
- **v5 stays out.** On top of the bursts its slower case is gone where it was (attract 1000, 1900, race 6040), and it
  shortens the geometry 0.01-0.06 everywhere (1450 43.1 -> 57.5 fps), but five polygon-RAM-heavy frames are slower
  than without it by 0.002-0.012 vblank (attract 1400, 1500 +0.009, 1650, 3000; Daytona 2 6400 +0.012, its DMA +0.011):
  r3d_mem's group bursts still wait a turn behind the store's posted writes. Against the base all are shorter; against
  the build without v5 they are not, so it fails the rule.
- **The measurement build** (`patches/cr3m-eccf1a0.patch`: eccf1a0 + row 6's Real3D value + v3 + the bursts, M3_FBUSY_BUILD
  on), gated (`--analyze_file` single and dual 8 of 8 clean; lint the base's 11 warnings) and fitted once:

  275 ALMs needed. RBF `cr3m_s1_e293533c.rbf` (e293533c4194a5be657ff08d5ef48a90). Not on the board yet.
- Row 6's first value on the board: DD SS WWWW, drops at the flip, swaps, and the longest swap wait in the second
  (units of 256 clocks, 227B a vblank). WWWW near a vblank at the start line would make the 2.00 frames the swap wait;
  small WWWW puts the hold outside r3d_cmd.

*On the board (2026-11-20).* `cr3m_s1` (e293533c: eccf1a0 + v3 + the polygon RAM bursts + row 6's drop / swap /
swap-wait counts; dual, 130 MHz) runs VF3, Scud Race, Daytona 2 and Sega Rally 2. At Sega Rally 2's start line row 6
reads DD 00, SS 1D-2C, WWWW 0000: the Real3D drops nothing and never holds the host there, yet each frame of the slow
second is exactly 2.00 vblank. That sent the start line back to the CPU side (D-78), and R192 then found it is the
game's own pacing after a short decrementer reload, not speed.


**R192 — The CPU on the race and the start line, measured: a replay bench runs Supermodel snapshots of Daytona 2's
race and Sega Rally 2's start line through the board's RTL (CPU, bus, DMA device, both SDRAMs, IRQ controller,
video timing, m3_frame_busy). Daytona 2's heavy race loops take 0.98 vblank at 130 MHz, where the 603e at 166 MHz
(Supermodel's CPI model with the manual's timings) needs about 0.41: one issue a clock (41% of our cycles), the FP
latencies (19%), memory (18%) and fetch bubbles (14.5%) are the gap. The CPI items (R174 / R188) take 3.4-3.6% off
the race frames, cycle for cycle as before. Nothing cheap gives D-78's -10%: the FP latencies are the FPGA's (the
manual's 3 / 4 cycles would give -7.4 to -8.4%), eight-entry micro-TLBs -1.5% for +583 ALM, a 256-entry BTB -0.3%.
And Sega Rally 2's start line is not the CPU's on this bench: 0.76-0.78 vblank with its DMA, under the game's own
deadline of 0.969, so D-78's reading of the board's 2.00-vblank frames is wrong.**

Work in `sm3-builds/cpu78/` (notes in `NOTES.md`; `tree` is eccf1a0 + r3d75's cr3m patch, the board's cr3m_s1;
`items/tree` the same with the CPI items). D-30, D-48 / D-57, D-52 / D-69, D-56, D-58, D-59, D-74-D-78; R171-R174,
R183, R185, R188-R191. Desk and bench only: nothing fitted, nothing on the board, nothing committed.

*What I believed:*
- R188 / D-78: Daytona 2's race (board 1.01-1.10 vblank, peaks 1.24-1.31) and Sega Rally 2's start line (board 2.00,
  "rest" 1.86) are both our CPU being slower than the boards' 603e, and the race needs about -10% (-25% at the worst
  corners).
- R191: SR2's start line is 0.94-1.05 vblank of CPU and DMA on the bench, right at the edge. That figure was a
  transfer: Supermodel's instructions at Daytona 2's cost per instruction.
- The race could only be reached by transfer (the system bench needs about 40 hours to get there, R185 / R188).

*What I know now:*

**1. The replay bench** (`bench/cpurep_tb.sv`, `bench/tb_cpurep.cpp`).
- My Supermodel copy writes a snapshot at the first execution of a chosen PC in chosen frames (every register, TB,
  DEC, the IRQ enable, the CROM bank, the cycles since IRQ 02, the 8 MiB of work RAM), and logs every CPU read outside
  RAM and CROM. Daytona 2: R171's race script, at the loop's start 4C764, frames 4500-8900 every 400. Sega Rally 2:
  sr2dma's script, at the pacing poll's exit 78898, the start line 5530-5800 every 30 and the race at 6000 / 6400.
- The bench is the RTL as Model3.sv builds it, dual (ppc_cpu ISB WV RPE; m3_bus Step 2 FAST R3P TGT W2 and the
  bridges pass; m3_scripts' DMA device; m3_sdr_port on m2_sdram; m3_sdr2; both SDRAMs at their pins; m2_video_timing;
  the time base; m3_frame_busy), with the MRA's SDRAM image for CROM. A stub at FFF00100 loads the registers, empties
  the TLBs and rfi's into the game when the video is at the snapshot's line. The IRQs, the decrementer and the DMA are
  the RTL's. The I/O board's and the security board's reads come from Supermodel's log, a queue per address; the
  Real3D's status word is r3d_cmd's; its host port is a 32-word FIFO drained a word every 12 clocks.
- Checks of the path: Supermodel's executed-PC list for the window (M3DIS) against the bench's retirements. Daytona 2
  runs 4 frames with no PC Supermodel did not run, TLB-miss handlers aside. Sega Rally 2's only departures are its
  DMA busy polls (Supermodel's DMA is instant) and one branch in the vblank handler. About 70 kHz: a frame in 32 s.
- Three faults of mine on the way (NOTES): the DMA device's configuration byte left at reset (the game
  read-modify-writes it: no move ever interrupted), Real3D status reads answered from Supermodel's log (the game polls
  the ping-pong bit at its loop's start, so the queue ran dry), and the 315-5649's byte given at its strobe rather than
  a clock before (every input read got the previous byte, and Daytona 2 left the race a frame later).

**2. The frames** (warm frames 2-4 of each snapshot, base RTL, 130 MHz; the board's measure):

|---|---|---|---|
| Daytona 2, 4500-7300 (7 snapshots) | 599-692 k | 0.875-0.982 | 0.025-0.046 |
| Daytona 2, 7700-8900 (4) | 427-467 k | 0.673-0.733 | 0.022-0.029 |
| Daytona 2, 5300 | 245 k | 0.378 | 0.027 |
| Sega Rally 2 start line, 5530-5800 (10) | 648-689 k | 0.76-0.78 | 0.103-0.107 |

Daytona 2's frame follows its loop's instruction count, 1.42e-6 vblank an instruction at 600-690 k. This scripted
race tops out at 691 k (p99): the board's 1.01-1.10 are loops of about 715-780 k, a race with the pack in view.

**3. Where the cycles go, against the 603e at 166 MHz.** Daytona 2 6100 (2.22 M clocks a frame at 130 MHz):

| cause | % of the frame | the 603e (manual) |
|---|---|---|
| issue, one uop a clock (branches included) | 41.1 | two a clock to different units, branches folded (6.3, 6.4.1.1): 21% fewer cycles than a single-issue 603e in Supermodel's model |
| FP dependency + FPU busy | 15.5 + 3.4 | single 1-1-1, double multiplies 2-1-1 (table 6-5) against this core's 6 (5 with the early forward) and 12; the bench at the manual's latencies: -7.4% |
| data wait | 12.2 (D fills 7.2, inside the D-cache 3.7) | 10.4 k D fills a frame, first word 17.8 clocks (137 ns); the 603e's on a 66 MHz MPC106 about 110-120 ns (desk) |
| fetch bubbles + redirects | 12.5 + 2.0 | a taken branch without a BTB hit costs 2-3 here, nothing on the 603e when its target is in the queue |
| I-miss | 5.7 | 5.0 k I fills, about 25 clocks exposed each |
| EX held other, load-use, mul/div | 4.6 + 2.4 + 0.4 | load-use 2 on both |
| of all the cycles: TLB-miss handlers | 6.8 (10.7% of the instructions; 3,800 DTLB load misses a frame, 58 clocks each) | the same handler and TLB geometry (64 entries, 2-way, 5.4.3.1): the same misses |

- Supermodel's CPI model with the 603e's options (dual dispatch, folding, the manual's FP latencies, 16 KiB 4-way
  caches, a 20-clock first word at 166 MHz) puts the same loop at 0.358 vblank, about 0.41 with the TLB handlers it
  does not run: 2.4x faster than this core at 130 MHz, 1.85x fewer cycles. Desk: a model, not the chip.
- By instruction class (`--pcprof`): integer loads CPI 3.67, FP loads 3.25, FP stores 3.21, single FP arithmetic
  2.69, double FP arithmetic 10.2, fcmpu 7.7 (it waits for its operands, not for serialisation), branches 1.27.
  The hottest code: a sine-table lookup (lfsx misses, 9-11 clocks a load), frsqrte and three Newton steps in double
  (a dependent chain at 13 clocks an op, 4.2% of the frame), fdivs into stfs (32 clocks).
- Sega Rally 2 5620: issue 40.1, FP dependency 18.6, EX held other 17.1 (a byte-scan loop at 6D38C, a load then its
  compare), data wait 8.8, fetch bubbles 5.2; no TLB misses (BAT-mapped); 7,060 uncached DMA busy polls a frame,
  22.7 clocks each. The 603e model: 0.333 vblank.

**4. Sega Rally 2's pacing, from its code** (the snapshot's RAM through ppcd; 787EC is called once a loop from
2DE8C, which drops its frame time):
- 78828: if [4C219C] is not 0, wait at 78834-78840 until it is (not one of m3_frame_busy's windows);
- 78868: if the count [4C2188] is 0 or below, reload it from [4C2184] (78874 / 78878);
- 7887C: if the count is above 0, poll 7888C-78894 until it is 0; 78898: reload it, and the next frame's work.
- [4C2184] is 1 at every snapshot (5530-6400): the game asks for 60. The count goes down in the vblank handler
  (IRQ 02); [4C219C] goes up in the decrementer handler (78C10; DEC reloaded at each IRQ 02 to 278,114 time-base
  ticks, 0.969 vblank) and is cleared in the vblank handler. So a frame whose work reaches 78828 later than 0.969
  vblank after its IRQ 02 waits for the next IRQ 02 and then, its count at 0, for one more: the plain pacing
  consequence, a full vblank lost for any lateness. There is no governor and no switch to 30.
- The deadline is 0.969 vblank of CPU and DMA from IRQ 02. The bench's start line is 0.76-0.78: 20% inside it.
- At 95 MHz (the same frames made late, `obj/rep_hz95`) the bench drops to 30 and m3_frame_busy reads 1.04-1.08,
  never 2.00: a late frame reads its own length. The board's frames of exactly 2.00 (and its 0.65-0.70 minima in the
  same seconds) need a hold of about a vblank outside the DMA polls, which this bench's ideal Real3D sink does not
  have. Not found; not the CPU.

- The FP latencies are what this fabric gives (about 1.4 ns a LUT level, routing-bound, R118 / ppc_fpu_fma's notes):
  a single FMA at the 603e's 3 cycles is about 7-8 levels a stage, near 100 MHz. Only latency hiding (the 603e's own
  FPU reservation station, 6.3.3: R171's +400-800 ALM est.) or dual issue (D-27) moves the FP-bound chains, and
  Daytona 2's are mostly FP-on-FP (sfma chains into fcmpu), which a reservation station does not overlap.
- HITRD on the work-RAM SDRAM (an open-row read from S_DISPATCH): -0.16% / -0.26%. Not worth m2_sdram's timing.
- The empty-ID cycles (cpi's fe_prof bound in; 20.4% of Daytona 2 6100's frame): the static rule's bc mispredicts
  4.5%, line-crossing I-misses 3.2%, taken branches with no BTB entry 2.8% (not capacity: the BTB is flushed at every
  tlbli, about 120 a frame), the MMU replay's refetch 2.8% (gone with RPX), a fill's beats 1.9%, rfi / sc /
  exception entries 1.4%, the instruction micro-TLB's refetch 1.1%. D-30 keeps the 603e's static rule, so the
  mispredicts are not a route; they are the chip's own, at a larger penalty here (EX against the BPU).

**7. Waits my RTL imposes that the board would not** (desk unless marked):
- One bus for both masters (m3_bus): a CPU miss waits while the DMA engine's transaction holds it, where the
  MPC106 keeps the 60x bus and PCI apart. Counted on the bench (`busdma`): 13.7-13.9 k clocks a Daytona 2 frame, 0.6%.
- The first word of a fill 17.8 clocks (137 ns), a line 25 clocks (192 ns), 32 bits a beat; the board's 603e on a
  64-bit 66 MHz bus about 110-120 ns and 150-165 ns.
- The DMA engine moves 20-25 MB/s (R189), a bursting PCI master about 55: Daytona 2's list wait 0.025-0.046 vblank.
- R114 (a CPU access to a non-SDRAM target waits for R3P to drain) is PCI's own ordering rule, not extra. The
  uncached reads (22.7 clocks, 175 ns) are not slower than a PCI read through the MPC106.
